title: Yara and the Horizon
premise: Coral Delacroix, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries, has spent twenty years outrunning the wreck of the Meridian and the avalanche that killed his sister aboard it. When his old rival Sable Voss hires his crew for the one job sworn off long ago—salvaging the Meridian's sealed hold before the glacier calving season opens the route for six tides only—Coral discovers the rival knows what's inside: their family's lost inheritance and proof of who really caused the disaster. Racing the salvage fleet across ice fields, Coral must decide whether memory is a burden or a map. In the end he reaches the hold first, learns his sister died saving others rather than causing the wreck, claims the inheritance on her terms, and walks out of the mountains no longer invisible—but free.
about_author: Odile Winterbourne is the pen name of a former expedition cook who spent a decade in high-altitude base camps listening to guides tell stories they swore never to repeat. She writes adventure fiction about people whose pasts are harder terrain than any mountain.

chapters.title: The Long Way Around
chapters.summary: Coral Delacroix guides a wealthy client through a pass he shouldn't legally enter, establishing his skill and his exile. His POV; the beat is controlled loneliness—he measures life in miles to avoid measuring it in years.

chapters.title: Blacklist
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: how Coral was banned from two countries after the Meridian disaster, and how he rebuilt as an underground guide. His POV; emotional beat of shame worn as armor.

chapters.title: A Letter with Ice on It
chapters.summary: Sable Voss's letter arrives offering a fortune for a six-tide window job. Coral burns it, then can't sleep. His POV; the beat is the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: The Crew That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Coral assembles his small crew: navigator Ilsa, riggers Tam and Bo, medic Ferro—each with their own reason for being unemployable. Coral's POV; warmth begins to crack his isolation.

chapters.title: What Voss Wants
chapters.summary: Voss appears in person, revealing the target: the Meridian, sealed in glacial ice, holding the Delacroix family's lost inheritance and documents. Coral refuses. His POV; anger masking terror.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Map
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals she's already charted the calving-season route—and that the salvage fleet has hired half the region's guides. The crew votes to take the job without him. Coral's POV; the beat of being outvoted by people who believe in him.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Planning chapter: the glacier will open the route briefly; the fleet leaves in three days. Coral finally agrees, setting rules: no talk of his sister. His POV; reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: Departure at Grey Light
chapters.summary: The crew departs ahead of the fleet via a smugglers' trail. Tense, quiet prose; Coral's POV; the beat of crossing a line he can't uncross.

chapters.title: The Smugglers' Toll
chapters.summary: Border runners demand payment the crew doesn't have; Coral bargains with information instead, exposing more of his past than he intended. His POV; vulnerability as currency.

chapters.title: First Tide
chapters.summary: They reach the ice shelf as the first tide rises; the route exists but barely. Ilsa's POV; awe and fear—the mountain indifferent to human deadlines.

chapters.title: Fleet Smoke on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Spotting the salvage fleet taking the main channel, faster than expected. Tam suggests sabotage; Coral forbids it. Coral's POV; the beat of choosing the kind of man he'll be.

chapters.title: Crevasse Field
chapters.summary: Bo falls into a crevasse; the rescue costs them six hours and nearly Bo's life. Ferro's POV; the crew bonds through crisis while the clock tightens.

chapters.title: Second Tide, Lost Ground
chapters.summary: A storm closes the route behind them—they cannot retreat. Ilsa's POV; dread transformed into resolve: forward is the only direction.

chapters.title: Voss's Second Letter
chapters.summary: A fleet scout delivers Voss's taunting letter: he knew Coral would come, and hints he knows what happened inside the Meridian. Coral's POV; paranoia and grief colliding.

chapters.title: The Sister in the Ice
chapters.summary: Extended flashback: Coral and his sister Maren planning the voyage that killed her, and the fight they had the night before. Coral's POV; the wound reopened deliberately.

chapters.title: Third Tide
chapters.summary: Halfway point; the crew celebrates too early and gets sloppy near a serac field. Tam's POV; hubris punished, trust tested.

chapters.title: The Turncoat
chapters.summary: They discover someone fed their route to the fleet—one of the border runners sold them. Coral suspects his own crew. His POV; the beat of suspicion poisoning fellowship.

chapters.title: Ferro's Confession
chapters.summary: Ferro admits sending a distress ping days ago to protect a sick Bo, unintentionally traceable. Not betrayal—fear. Coral's POV; relief and self-reproach for doubting them.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: The Narrow Way
chapters.summary: The route narrows to a single rope-line traverse above open water. Ilsa leads; Coral follows her orders for the first time. Ilsa's POV; leadership passed like a torch.

chapters.title: The Fleet Gains
chapters.summary: Voss's lead ship appears below them, using the channel they refused to sabotage. One tide of advantage left. Coral's POV; the cost of integrity made concrete.

chapters.title: Night Camp at the Calving Wall
chapters.summary: Camp beneath the glacier face; the ice groans all night. Crew members share why they're each unemployable. Multiple voices via Coral's listening POV; intimacy earned.

chapters.title: Maren's Journal
chapters.summary: Among Coral's gear, Ilsa finds the journal he's carried twenty years and never opened past page one. She returns it unread. Coral's POV; the choice to finally read begins.

chapters.title: Reading by Stove-Light
chapters.summary: Coral reads Maren's journal entries about the Meridian's cargo and a passenger list that contradicts the official story. His hands shake. His POV; memory reframing itself.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: The final usable tide; they sprint the last ice bridge as the fleet lands behind them. Race chapters begin. Bo's POV; exhilaration burning off fear.

chapters.title: The Wreck Appears
chapters.summary: The Meridian emerges from retreating ice, preserved and terrible. Coral sees the hull where his sister died. His POV; grief given a physical address.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Coral, Ilsa, and Tam board through a fissure; the interior is a frozen museum of the disaster. Coral's POV; walking through his worst memory.

chapters.title: The Sealed Hold
chapters.summary: They reach the hold door—welded shut from the inside. Someone sealed it during the sinking. Mystery deepens. Tam's POV; dawning realization this wasn't simple tragedy.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Voss and his team breach the wreck from the seaward side; confrontation in the corridors. Voss reveals he was Maren's crewmate that night. Coral's POV; rage and revelation tangled.

chapters.title: What Maren Did
chapters.summary: Voss testifies: the sinking was caused by the shipping company smuggling unstable cargo; Maren welded the hold to contain it and saved eleven lives before the ice took her. Coral's POV; twenty years of guilt collapsing into truth.

chapters.title: The Fleet Closes
chapters.summary: Voss's backers arrive to seize everything—including the exculpatory documents. Voss, unexpectedly, sides with Coral against his own employers. Coral's POV; enemy becoming ally.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: The glacier begins to calve; the wreck and route are doomed. Escape becomes the new race. Ilsa's POV; the mountain reclaiming its dead.

chapters.title: The Hold's Last Secret
chapters.summary: Inside the hold: the inheritance is not gold but Maren's evidence archive plus the family deed Voss truly wanted. Coral chooses the truth over the treasure. His POV; values clarified under pressure.

chapters.title: Running the White Road
chapters.summary: Desperate escape across collapsing ice as calving walls fall behind them; Bo injured again, carried. Ferro's POV; every hand matters.

chapters.title: The Bridge Goes
chapters.summary: The final ice bridge calves with Voss still crossing; Coral goes back for him against all logic and pulls him from the water. Coral's POV; the rival debt repaid across twenty years.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide: Last Window
chapters.summary: They make the far shore as the route seals behind them forever, the Meridian entombed. Headcount: everyone alive. Coral's POV; survival as grace.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: In a coastal town, Coral files Maren's documents with maritime authorities, ending his own blacklist by ending the lie that required it. His POV; justice as quiet paperwork.

chapters.title: What the Inheritance Buys
chapters.summary: The crew divides the salvage rights; Coral funds a rescue-training school in Maren's name. Each character's next path sketched. Coral's POV; legacy chosen, not inherited blindly.

chapters.title: Voss at the Dock
chapters.summary: Final conversation with Voss—not forgiveness exactly, but release. Two men who measured themselves against each other stop measuring. Coral's POV; rivalry dissolved into respect.

chapters.title: Yara and the Horizon
chapters.summary: Coral names the school Yara—Maren's middle name—and leads his first legal expedition toward the horizon, no longer counting miles to escape years but to spend them. His POV; homecoming to himself.
